item.text:
Bottom line: **mixed evidence, leaning only modestly positive for 8B.6**. In 2024, Sisi did convert some declarations into observable action in macroeconomic policy, targeted welfare, cabinet staffing, and Gaza mediation. But the broader political/security record still looks slogan-heavy and coercive: independent reporting shows continued arrests, censorship, and insider-controlled security institutions, with only limited, partial reforms.

**Supports 8B.6**
- **IMF Reaches Staff Level Agreement on the Third Review of the Extended Fund Facility with Egypt** — IMF, June 6, 2024, [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/06/pr-24208-egypt-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-3rd-review-of-the-eff) — The IMF says Egypt stayed the course on fiscal discipline, tight monetary policy, a flexible exchange-rate regime, and structural reforms, with improving FX availability and inflation easing. This is concrete implementation, not just declaration. `8B.6`
- **IMF Executive Board Completes the Third Review of the Extended Arrangement Under the Extended Fund Facility for Egypt** — IMF, July 29, 2024, [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/29/pr24293-egypt-imf-exec-board-completes-3rd-rev-extended-arr-eff) — The board said inflation was abating, FX shortages were eliminated, fiscal targets were met, and the program was continuing. That is observable state capacity and follow-through. `8B.6`
- **Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt Through Cash Transfer Programs** — World Bank Group, May 28, 2024, [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs) — Takaful and Karama is described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and run through proxy means testing, a grievance mechanism, and a dynamic registry, with a 55 percent benefit increase. This is a strong case of policy turning into delivery machinery. `8B.6`
- **President El-Sisi Meets Prime Minister and Members of the New Government** — State Information Service, July 3, 2024, [URL](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/) — Sisi told the new government to strengthen institutional frameworks, coordination, integrity, and transparency. Combined with the technocratic cabinet reshuffle, this is concrete personnel-and-instruction evidence. `8B.6`
- **Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, President Joe Biden, and Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani Joint Statement** — Presidency of the Republic of Egypt, August 8, 2024, [URL](https://www.presidency.eg/EN/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news882024-3/) — Egypt co-led a bridging proposal for a Gaza ceasefire and hostage-release deal and called for implementation. That is a visible diplomatic mechanism, not just rhetoric. `8B.6`
- **IAEA General Conference Adopts Egypt’s Resolution on Applying Comprehensive Safeguards to All Nuclear Facilities in the Middle East** — Egypt Ministry of Foreign Affairs, September 19, 2024, [URL](https://www.mfa.gov.eg/ar/Ministers/Details/MinistryNews/188) — Egypt used its diplomatic position to push a specific nonproliferation resolution. This shows state reach through formal institutions. `8B.6`
- **Sisi Directs the Government to Shorten Pretrial Detention and Activate Alternatives** — Presidency of the Republic of Egypt, August 21, 2024, [URL](https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/news2182024/) — This is the clearest official procedural-reform signal I found: a public instruction to alter detention practice, not just praise reform. `8B.6`

**Cuts against 8B.6**
- **Egypt: Civic Space Under Siege** — Human Rights Watch, January 11, 2024, [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/egypt-civic-space-under-siege) — HRW says the government curbed free expression and assembly, failed to ensure economic rights, and did not take concrete transparency/civilian-oversight measures. This is strong evidence that many declarations did not translate into rights-preserving implementation. `8B.6`
- **Egypt: Court Punishes Activists Challenging al-Sisi** — Human Rights Watch, February 8, 2024, [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/08/egypt-court-punishes-activists-challenging-al-sisi) — The sentencing and election ban for Tantawy and supporters show legal machinery being used to suppress challenge, not to open the political field. `8B.6`
- **Egypt: More Than 100 Arbitrarily Detained Over Calls for Anti-Government Protests** — Amnesty International, July 18, 2024, [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/) — Amnesty documents mass arrests over protest calls tied to prices and power cuts. That is coercive state reach, but not the kind that reflects implemented public-purpose reform. `8B.6`
- **Egypt’s Sisi Names New Armed Forces Chief of Staff, Defence Minister** — Reuters via Yahoo, July 3, 2024, [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/egypts-sisi-names-ex-defence-140545714.html) — The reshuffle replaced senior security officials but recycled them into adviser roles. That looks like managed insider rotation, not depersonalized institutional reform. `8B.6`
- **Egypt’s Sisi Replaces Head of Powerful General Intelligence Agency** — Reuters via Yahoo, October 16, 2024, [URL](https://www.yahoo.com/news/egypt-sisi-appoints-head-general-145312663.html) — Reuters says the intelligence service remained tied to domestic-security repression while leadership stayed within the same close network. This cuts against a clean “implementation through neutral institutions” reading. `8B.6`
- **Egypt: Authorities Must End Campaign of Mass Arrests and Forced Returns of Sudanese Refugees** — Amnesty International, June 19, 2024, [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/egypt-authorities-must-end-campaign-of-mass-arrests-and-forced-returns-of-sudanese-refugees/) — Border forces and police mass-arrested refugees and forced returns without asylum access. That is observable state reach, but in a punitive and rights-violating form. `8B.6`

**Search gap**
- I found **clear implementation evidence in economics, welfare, and diplomacy**, but **little independent proof that Sisi’s 2024 “reform” language produced durable institutional change** beyond IMF-monitored macro policy and a few official procedural moves.
- The strongest pro-implementation items are often **official Egyptian statements or externally supervised program documents**; the strongest contrary items are **independent rights reports**.
- I did **not** find solid independent evidence that the July 2024 cabinet reshuffle or August pretrial-detention directive produced broad, sustained downstream change by year-end.
